# Hidden property in Font class returns inverted value

## Description

I've discovered an issue with the `hidden` property in the `Font` class. When trying to check if text is hidden, the property returns the opposite of what it should.

## Expected Result

When text is marked as hidden in a Word document, the `hidden` property should return `True`. When text is not hidden, it should return `False`.

## Actual Result

The property returns the opposite value - `True` when text is not hidden and `False` when it is hidden.

## Reproduction Steps

```python
from docx import Document

# Create a document
doc = Document()
p = doc.add_paragraph()
run = p.add_run("This text should be hidden")

# Set the text to be hidden
run.font.hidden = True

# Check if the text is hidden
print(f"Is text hidden? {run.font.hidden}")  # Should print True but prints False

# Set the text to be visible
run.font.hidden = False

# Check if the text is hidden
print(f"Is text hidden? {run.font.hidden}")  # Should print False but prints True
```

This issue affects any code that relies on checking the hidden state of text in a document, potentially causing hidden text to be treated as visible and vice versa.
</issue>
